nonblocking: N1 (Q1, uncovered invariant): the `and not finished()` guard (intake.py:423) has no mutant in the lane's list. The verifier's mutant `drain_ignores_finished` (remove `and not finished()`) SURVIVES the lane's G suite (its sibling `watched_ignores_more_body`, done set only on a non-http.request message, was not surveyed against the lane suite; same mechanism) - under the in-process TestClient/ASGITransport a spurious drain parks on a receive until the 30 s window and the refusal then passes, only slowly (lane's G suite from a copy of the d502c90 tree (tests/g minus jobs/, test_mutants.py, and the two repo-relative client files): pristine copy 9 failed, 468 passed in 37.71s; under drain_ignores_finished the SAME 9 failures (all layout-only: tests/g/ops/test_mutants.py x8 + test_publication.py), 468 passed in 425.34s - the mutant survives; ten post-read refusals stall ~30 s each and still pass (e.g. 30.04s test_admission.py::test_dur_cap__denied_capacity_is_retryable_and_the_retry_is_admitted_once, 30.06s test_structure.py::test_media_sec__the_separator_cap_is_exact, 32.72s uploads test_the_named_cases_pass_on_the_pristine_tree); test_validate.py alone 105 passed in 0.96s; uploads/test_uploads.py 27 passed in 30.78s; test_structure.py in 6 shards 65 passed (60.65 s / 150.99 s / 30.49 s on the stalling shards). Logs /tmp/claude-1000/drain-chk-logs/suite-*.log, sshard-0*.log). Both are killed by the verifier's case test_v__a_refusal_after_the_whole_body_is_answered_at_once (real socket: full body sent, `accept` refuses 429 Retry-After 5; mutant: `AssertionError: b'' / assert (0 == 429)`, the answer parked past the 3 s client timeout) and test_v__a_second_request_object_reads_through_the_guard (TimeoutError from wait_for(2 s)). Recommend adding the first case to tests/g/test_intake_drain.py plus a `drain_after_the_body_ended` mutant. The code itself is correct: finished() flips on the more_body=False message seen through the guard's receive (intake.py:286-296), every handler reads through the Request built at intake.py:420, and jobs._as_async (jobs.py:206) builds its second Request from `request.receive`, which IS that watched receive - no bypass (proved by the second case).

N2 (Q2, two bounds without a killing mutant): `while total <= declared` (drain loop) - the verifier's mutant `while True` is unreachable under h11 framing (the lane's six real-socket cases pass) and under test_structure's fake receive (which never suspends) it spins forever: a hang, not an assertion death (the runner would call it broken_runner). Defence-in-depth only; h11 ends the body at Content-Length. `except Exception: return` - mutant `drain_exceptions_escape` (except ZeroDivisionError) IS killed by the lane's window case: `AssertionError: b'HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error ...'` (the TimeoutError escapes the guard's except-DomainError block).

N3 (Q7, rollout row understates memory): the lane's 3.00x reproduces exactly for its pipeline (read_body -> decode_utf8 -> check_structure -> parse_object: 3.00 MiB -> 9.01 MiB peak; 95.00 MiB -> 285.01 MiB peak, 0.41 s), but the large-body slot is held across the whole `Ingress.validated` (released in its finally, ingress.py:162-172: normalize + identity_digest run under it); measured through `validated`: 3 MiB -> 12.12 MiB (4.04x), 85 MiB -> 340.12 MiB (4.00x, 0.53 s), 95 MiB -> 380.12 MiB (4.00x, 0.59 s). Worst case at LARGE_BODY_LIMIT=8 is therefore 8 x 96 MiB x 4 = 3,072 MiB (not 2,304) and ~8 x 0.59 = 4.7 s of loop stall (not 3.6 s). Still inside the gateway's `--memory 8g` (marlin2b-gateway.service:27) with ~4.9 GiB headroom, so 8 remains safe; the row should say 4x / 3,072 MiB / ~4.7 s. Payloads already past the slot (in `accept`) are outside this model (pre-existing, ingress.py:166-171 comment).

N4 (Q8, proposal overclaims): the proposal's last sentence 'Overload refusals stay 429 with Retry-After and an overload code; the connection is never reused after one' is false for `rate_limited` and `journal_capacity_exhausted` (429 overload codes not in CLOSE_CODES, intake.py:55-56; they keep the connection). Also 'a window that ends first is answered and closed without draining' - the body IS drained until the window ends, then cut. And 'never make the gateway read a video' - a pilot clip can be under 1 MiB; the bound is bytes. Corrected wording in ruling_text.

N5 (behaviour change, lane's Limits already names it): `Expect: 100-continue`. Measured on a raw socket, gate refusal of a 3 MB declared body: with the drain the client's first read is `HTTP/1.1 100 Continue` (0.003 s), it uploads 3 MB, then reads the 429 (0.006 s); without the drain (refusal_not_drained tree) its first read is the 429 before any body byte. So a 100-continue client (curl sends Expect for bodies > 1 MiB) now uploads up to 96 MiB before a refusal it could have read for free. Bounded and correct; the pilot's httpx clients and the Caddy hop do not use Expect. Cheap follow-up: skip the drain when `expect: 100-continue` and no receive has happened yet.

N6 (DoS surface, Q3): memory is bounded - chunks are counted, never kept (8 x 96 MiB drained over real sockets in parallel: traced peak 2.37 MiB; the accumulating mutant `drain_keeps_chunks`: 769.18 MiB; in-process 8 x 96 MiB drain(): 0.59 MiB vs mutant 768.51 MiB, the verifier case test_v__a_drain_keeps_nothing kills it: `AssertionError: 768.5 MiB kept`); uvicorn's h11 pauses reading past 64 KiB buffered (uvicorn/protocols/http/h11_impl.py:266-267, HIGH_WATER_LIMIT flow_control.py:7). What the drain does add is time: a refused connection (anonymous: <= 1 MiB declared; authenticated: <= 96 MiB) can now be held until INTAKE_TIMEOUT_S (30 s) by a trickling client instead of closing at once. No new memory class and no new unauthenticated byte volume beyond 1 MiB; uvicorn has no --limit-concurrency in the unit (marlin2b-gateway.service:31-33) and slow headers could already hold a connection, so not blocking; worth a line in the ruling's rationale or the runbook.

N7 (uploads): the drain bound on PUT is MAX_REQUEST_BYTES (96 MiB) while the PUT read is cut at MAX_MEDIA_BYTES (64 MiB, uploads.py:133): a PUT declaring 80 MiB is read to 64 MiB, refused request_too_large, then drained ~16 MiB more. Bounded by the same window; consistent with the proposed ruling text. Informational.
N8 (harness hygiene, not the lane's): the lane's claim 'contracts quick: not run' is now covered (1039 passed at d502c90).

A refusal after a full read therefore drains nothing: real socket, 429 Retry-After 5 from accept after the full SMALL and 3 MB bodies, answered < 3 s with window 30 s (verifier case passes at d502c90). jobs._as_async (jobs.py:201-206) re-wraps `request.receive` of the guard-built Request = the watched receive: in-process case with a receive that parks after the last message returns 429 with exactly 2 receives. Mutants removing `not finished()` or the more_body test die in both verifier cases, but survive the lane's suite (N1).

ruling_text: | R108 | A connection-closing refusal first drains a declared body, within the intake bounds (INTAKE-DRAIN; verifier wording) | When the gateway answers a request on the chat ingress, `POST /v1/jobs` or an upload route with a code that closes the connection (`invalid_api_key`, `request_too_large`, `capacity_exhausted`, `deadline_exceeded`) before that request's body has been read to its end, it first reads and discards the rest of the body, and only when the request declares a `Content-Length` of at most `MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` (for `invalid_api_key`, at most 1 MiB: a caller with no valid key can never make the gateway read more). The drain stops at the first of: the end of the declared body, a receive error or disconnect, and the end of the `INTAKE_TIMEOUT_S` window that began when the route received the request, so it never makes a refusal later than that window. The answer is then the typed envelope with `Connection: close`, and the connection is never reused. A chunked body or a declared length over the bound is answered and closed at once, and a body still arriving when the window ends is cut there; such a caller may lose the refusal to a reset, so a client that must read its refusals declares the length. A refusal raised after the body was read to its end drains nothing. Drained bytes are counted, never kept or parsed. Codes outside this set are unchanged: `rate_limited` and `journal_capacity_exhausted` keep the connection. |
